description: Aggregate paths that coverage showed untested: the linear-regression family over the exact line y = 2x + 1 (every REGR_ statistic a clean constant, with NULL-bearing pairs skipped and a single usable pair leaving the slope undefined), MAX_BY / MIN_BY in both the scalar and top-N array forms with NULL sort keys never winning, the single-row and all-NULL edges of the statistical aggregates (sample statistics need n >= 2), and the GENERATOR / SPLIT_TO_TABLE table functions with their full output column sets including the LATERAL per-row form. Converted 1:1 from functions/AggregateGapCoverageTest (now retired); its @BeforeEach pts fixture is inlined per test and the 1e-9 tolerances are supplied by the testkit's numeric normalisation.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE pts (x INTEGER, y INTEGER)
SELECT REGR_SLOPE(y, x), REGR_INTERCEPT(y, x), REGR_R2(y, x), REGR_COUNT(y, x), REGR_AVGX(y, x), REGR_AVGY(y, x) FROM pts
CREATE TABLE pts (x INTEGER, y INTEGER)
SELECT REGR_SXX(y, x), REGR_SYY(y, x), REGR_SXY(y, x) FROM pts
SELECT REGR_SLOPE(y, x) FROM pts WHERE x = 1
CREATE TABLE emp (name VARCHAR, pay INTEGER)
SELECT SEQ4() AS s FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 4)) ORDER BY s
SELECT t.seq, t.index, t.value FROM TABLE(SPLIT_TO_TABLE('a,b,c', ',')) t ORDER BY t.index
SELECT t.index, t.value FROM TABLE(SPLIT_TO_TABLE('a,b,c', ',')) t ORDER BY t.index
CREATE TABLE csvs (id INTEGER, s VARCHAR)
SELECT c.id, t.value FROM csvs c, LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(c.s, ',') t ORDER BY c.id, t.index
